metadata.product_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Jobs to be Done
metadata.objective: Understand what jobs health-conscious adults 18-35 are trying to accomplish when they reach for a sugar-free carbonated beverage — functional jobs (power through the 2pm desk slump without another coffee, substitute for a beer at a rooftop bar, scratch the soda craving without a calorie hit), emotional jobs (feel indulgent without guilt, feel alert without jittery, feel like the kind of person who reads labels), and social jobs (have an adult-coded drink in hand while friends are doing Dry January, signal wellness alignment without preaching). Probe the pains driving switching — sweetener aftertaste fatigue, a TikTok creator calling out an ingredient, price creep, availability drops at their usual grocery. Elicit desired outcomes — clean energy, recognizable short-label ingredients, a flavor that doesn't get boring. Treat Coke Zero, Celsius, LaCroix, and Olipop as category alternatives respondents are hiring against.

turns.question: I'd love to hear about your experience with drinks—you know, those moments when you reach for something to drink during the day. Can you think back to the last time in the past week or so when you grabbed a beverage and it felt like the right choice for that moment? Walk me through what was going on and what made you pick that particular drink.
turns.response: I grabbed an iced coffee this morning before work because I needed the caffeine kick, honestly. I was running late and just wanted something cold that would actually wake me up. Coffee does that better than anything else for me, so it was kind of an automatic reach.

turns.question: When you reach for coffee like this morning, what would it feel like if you weren't sure it would actually wake you up?
turns.response: Honestly that would be pretty frustrating. Like, I'm already groggy and just want something that actually works, not something I have to wonder about. I'd probably just grab something else instead of wasting time on a maybe.
